thread.title: Qualcomm: Still Worth Holding as a Value Stock, Says RBC

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Qualcomm: Still Worth Holding as a Value Stock, Says RBC
text:
What do you do with Qualcomm ( QCOM ) after Broadcom ’s ( AVGO ) hostile bid was shot down last week by the U.S. government?
It’s still one to buy, according to a note today from Amit Daryanani with RBC Capital Markets , reiterating his Outperform rating on the name, and his $80 price target.
It’s a good value stock, Daryanani argues. He doesn’t exactly believe management’s boast it can reach $6.75 to $7.50 in earnings per share come fiscal 2019. (Neither does the Street: the average estimate according to FactSet is $3.77.) That’s “optimistic,” in his view.
But he believes the company can get to $6.25 to $6.50, and with a multiple of 12 to 14 times, "this would peg QCOM stock in the $75-90 range with a 3.8% yield."
In addition, Daryanani likes several “tailwinds” for the stock.
They include accretion from the purchase of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), assuming its approved by China’s regulatory authority, MOFCOM .” That alone is expected to add about $1.30 to $1.50 a share in EPS.
A resolution of the company’s dispute with China’s Huawei could add another 20 cents to 30 cents per share in profit. If the company can reach a settlement with Apple ( AAPL ) in the ongoing patent royalties dispute between the two, it would add yet another 55 cents to 65 cents per share to earnings.
And then there’s the "potential for picking back baseband allocation post AAPL resolution,” that might give Qualcomm another 5 cents to 10 cents a share, he figures.
Daryanani makes a plea for investors to keep the faith despite the recent history of the company:
While we understand historical execution has been choppy, we think there is high probability that OEMs under dispute may settle sooner now that its clear QCOM isn’t going anywhere. Furthermore, should we get more discipline and consistent execution the stock should see a sustained multiple expansion.
Qualcomm shares today ended the session down $1.45, or 2.5%, at $56.81.
